subject: history
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: From which region of Scandinavia did the Vikings who raided Britain mainly come?
questions.explain: The Vikings who raided and settled Britain came mainly from Norway and Denmark.

questions.q: The 878 treaty between Alfred and Guthrum chiefly did what?
options: Gave the Vikings all of Wessex
Divided England between Saxon and Viking control
questions.explain: The peace after Edington, formalised by treaty, set a boundary dividing English and Viking (Danelaw) areas.

questions.q: What was the chief Norse god, associated with war and wisdom?
questions.explain: Odin was the chief god of the Norse, linked with war, wisdom and the dead in Valhalla.

questions.q: What was a Viking 'jarl'?
questions.explain: A jarl was a Viking noble or chieftain at the top of free Viking society, above karls and thralls.

questions.q: Which Viking ruler became king of all England in 1016?
questions.explain: Cnut (Canute) became King of England in 1016 and ruled a North Sea empire.

questions.q: Which place did Viking warriors who died bravely in battle hope to reach?
questions.explain: Vikings believed slain warriors were taken to Valhalla, the hall of the god Odin.

questions.q: Many Viking warriors were buried with their possessions, and important leaders sometimes in what?
questions.explain: High-status Vikings were sometimes buried in ships or graves outlined with stones in a ship shape, with grave goods.

questions.q: What were the Viking longships especially well suited for?
options: Fast sea voyages and shallow-water landings
questions.explain: Longships were fast, flexible and shallow-draughted, ideal for open sea and surprise coastal raids.

questions.q: The large Viking force that invaded England from 865 is usually known as what?
questions.explain: The Great Heathen Army landed in 865 and conquered much of Anglo-Saxon England.

questions.q: The Viking raid on Lindisfarne, often seen as the start of the Viking Age, took place in which year?
questions.explain: The raid on the monastery of Lindisfarne in 793 is traditionally regarded as the start of the Viking Age in Britain.

questions.q: Which Viking explorer is traditionally credited with reaching Vinland in North America around 1000?
questions.explain: Leif Erikson, son of Erik the Red, is credited with reaching Vinland in North America around the year 1000.

questions.q: What name was given to the area of England under Viking law and control?
questions.explain: The Danelaw was the region of England where Danish (Viking) law and customs prevailed.

questions.q: Which North Atlantic island did the Vikings settle from around the late 9th century?
questions.explain: Vikings settled Iceland from around 870 onwards, establishing farms and a system of assemblies.

questions.q: Which Anglo-Saxon king of Wessex resisted the Vikings and is called 'the Great'?
questions.explain: Alfred the Great of Wessex resisted the Viking Great Heathen Army and is the only English king called 'the Great'.

questions.q: In 878 Alfred defeated the Viking leader Guthrum at which battle?
questions.explain: Alfred's victory at the Battle of Edington in 878 forced Guthrum to make peace and accept baptism.

questions.q: Which major northern English city became an important Viking trading centre?
questions.explain: York, known to the Vikings as Jorvik, became a major Viking-ruled trading city.

questions.q: Why did the Vikings often target monasteries such as Lindisfarne?
options: They held wealth and were poorly defended
questions.explain: Monasteries held gold, silver and treasures yet were largely undefended, making them easy, rich targets.

questions.q: The word 'Viking' is often linked to a term meaning what?
questions.explain: 'Viking' is commonly associated with going on a raid or expedition, linked to the Norse word for piracy.

questions.q: What was a 'thing' (or 'thing-m(o)t') in Viking society?
options: An assembly where free men made laws and settled disputes
questions.explain: A 'thing' was a Viking assembly of free men that made laws and settled legal disputes.

questions.q: What was the social rank of most ordinary free Viking farmers, between jarls and thralls?
questions.explain: Karls were the free farmers and craftsmen, ranking below noble jarls and above enslaved thralls.

questions.q: As well as raiding, what other activity were the Vikings heavily involved in?
questions.explain: Vikings were extensive traders, dealing in furs, slaves, silver and goods from Russia to the Middle East.

questions.q: Cnut, who became king of England in 1016, also ruled which other kingdom?
questions.explain: Cnut ruled a North Sea empire that included England, Denmark and later Norway.
